title: Lightweight event fanout + checkpoint API for Python streaming chat ergonomics
text:
Lightweight event fanout + checkpoint API for Python streaming chat ergonomics

description:
Problem: customers build resilient streaming chat UIs and server-side consumers but repeatedly re-implement resume, backpressure and retry logic. Current SDK primitives are low-level (raw event streams) and produce varied patterns across apps. This ticket introduces a small, opinionated higher-level facade for Python that (1) provides a fanout-friendly event adapter that lets multiple consumers subscribe to typed events without duplicating network reads, (2) a soft checkpoint API (resume token + idempotent boundary markers) for resumability across transient disconnects, and (3) a retry-coalescing strategy that reduces duplicate downstream work during quick reconnect storms. Goals: reduce customer code by providing a single tested pattern, offer clear telemetry hooks (watermarks and retry reasons), and ship examples and migration docs. This is intentionally ergonomic: a synchronous iterator facade over an asyncio-native runner and clear adapter points for custom sinks (Kafka, HTTP fanout, in-process broadcaster).

acceptance_criteria:
SDK exposes an EventFanoutAdapter with subscribe/unsubscribe semantics and typed event callbacks
SoftCheckpoint object (opaque string token) persisted by caller can resume a stream with no duplicate application-level side-effects for idempotent sinks
Retry coalescing configurable (window default 500ms) and documented; tests verify no duplicate events delivered to idempotent handler when reconnects occur within window
Synchronous iterator facade available for sync user code and an asyncio-native AsyncEventIterator for async consumers
Comprehensive unit + integration tests covering resume, partial-emit, backpressure when consumer is slower than producer
Documentation page and two cookbook examples (one web frontend incremental UI, one server-side Kafka sink) published in docs repo
Telemetry hooks emitting: stream_start, checkpoint_resume, resume_token_renew, retry_coalesce, consumer_backpressure with token-level IDs

implementation_plan:
1) Define minimal Event type contract (kind, data, seq, optional boundary_id) and SoftCheckpoint token shape
2) Implement internal reader loop that decodes server SSE/HTTP-chunked events into typed events and publishes to a single in-process broadcaster
3) Build EventFanoutAdapter that maintains weak-subscriber refs and backpressure signals; make push non-blocking with bounded queue and overflow policy configurable (drop_oldest|block|error)
4) Implement ResumeCoordinator which handles SoftCheckpoint -> server query param, validates server ack boundary, and returns new resume_token on success
5) Add RetryCoalescer around resume path that suppresses immediate duplicate resume attempts for configured window; surface metrics and last-retry-reason
6) Provide two facades: SyncEventIterator (wraps broadcaster + thread-runner) and AsyncEventIterator (async generator), keep API parity with examples
7) Add tests: unit for parser and adapter, flakey-network integration bringing server simulator; add perf microbench for fanout 1..32 subscribers
8) Docs + cookbooks + SDK CHANGELOG entry; mark experimental in release notes
9) Release in py-sdk-2.6-beta, monitor telemetry for first 48 hours and be ready for quick patch

test_plan:
Unit: event framing/parsing fuzz tests, checkpoint encoding/decoding
Unit: adapter subscriber lifecycle: subscribe, process, unsubscribe under concurrent load
Integration: simulated server with intermittent disconnects, verify ResumeCoordinator avoids duplicates and resumes within 1 second under normal conditions
Integration: consumer backpressure test where slow consumer triggers configured overflow policy
E2E: cookbook examples executed in CI; web UI incremental updates show ordered partial tokens without duplication
Performance: fanout throughput test with 1k events/s and 16 subscribers, measure median publish-latency and tail latencies
Telemetry: assert that events stream_start/checkpoint_resume/retry_coalesce emitted to metrics backend during tests

notes:
2026-02-05 - Aisha: kicked off spike to validate resume_token semantics against server API; server team confirmed 'boundary_id' is returned on ack when a resume token matches a flushed KV cache boundary
2026-02-18 - Jonas: prototyped EventFanoutAdapter using asyncio.Queue + weakrefs; initial microbench shows 12% CPU overhead for 8 subscribers (acceptable)
2026-02-24 - Design review with Priya Shah and Diego Navarro: agreed to keep public API minimal (no automatic dedupe of non-idempotent handlers), designers want a clear UX for resume failure surfaces
2026-02-27 - Security: quick perf review; no sensitive data stored in checkpoint tokens (tokens are HMAC’ed with service key), security OK to proceed (formal review not required)
2026-03-03 - PM feedback: add coalescing window config and surface default of 500ms; add opt-in flag for 'strict-ordering' that disables coalescing for low-throughput strict-order use cases
2026-03-07 - Code review: core adapter and parser PR open, requesting stronger docs and two cookbooks; reviewers asked for clearer examples for synchronous iterator use in Flask-style apps
2026-03-10 - Jonas: merged parser and fanout core into feature branch; starting work on ResumeCoordinator and retries

example_usage:
# sync example (Flask)
from redwood_sdk.streaming import SyncEventIterator
# create iterator for chat completion stream and resume token storage handled by app
iter = SyncEventIterator(model='redwood-chat-large', resume_token_store=lambda: load_token())
for event in iter:
    if event.kind == 'delta':
        render_incremental(event.data)
    elif event.kind == 'boundary':
        save_token(event.checkpoint_token)

# async example (server consumer)
async def consumer():
    async for ev in AsyncEventIterator('redwood-chat-large'):
        await sink_to_kafka(ev)
